correctness.rationale: Under an explicit increasing conjugacy, direction signs are threshold observations of the full tent map. Three Markov cells enumerate exactly two disjoint return branches per minus gap, of inverse slope 2^-k. Count and diameter of all nested fibers are exact, yielding the frequency upper bound and, by the equal-weight Frostman construction and j/n_(j+1)->p, the lower bound for every p>0. Dimension zero at p=0 and the typical p=1/3 follow separately. The exact-rational checker ran 2234 finite assertions; none are used as an infinite proof. Boundary and conjugacy qualifications are explicit.

originality.rationale: The novel assessed statement is the exact Hausdorff dimension of every full infinite strict-direction observation fiber, equal to its minus frequency, and the almost-sure dimension 1/3. The prior 2001 paper proves nonuniqueness but does not state this frequency-resolved dimension law in its inspected full text. Pfante et al. analyze the same threshold in symbolic/information theory; their complete manuscript was inaccessible and is an explicit historical priority risk. Searches of the published results and own earlier claims did not expose a theorem whose hypotheses imply the fiber formula; the sign Markov chain and entropy are not claimed as new.

value.rationale: A natural complete-observation identifiability question has an exact answer: a typical infinite stream of only up/down logistic differences leaves a 1/3-dimensional set of possible initial states. The formula depends on the observed long-run down frequency and spans every admissible frequency p, rather than being a finite census, a generic entropy restatement, or a qualitative nonuniqueness remark. It distinguishes geometric reconstruction ambiguity from the established symbolic entropy and gives a precise observable invariant for coarse-graining.
